Graduate Assistantships
Graduate Assistantships provide students with valuable professional experience while supporting their academic goals. Roles may include teaching, research, or administrative responsibilities. Assistants receive tuition remission and/or a stipend as part of their appointment. Learn more and find resources for current assistants.
How to Apply
Step 1: Confirm your interest and join the applicant pool
New students: Apply through the “Next Steps” tab in your application portal. Once submitted, your application will be added to the applicant pool for departments that are hiring.
Continuing students: Email gradstudentservices@montclair.edu to confirm your interest.
Step 2: Reach out to your department for available opportunities
Reach out to your program contact or department chair to ask about potential assistantship opportunities, as each department handles the interview and selection process directly.
When reaching out, it can be helpful to include an updated resume, a brief personal statement and a recommendation letter.
Please note: Assistantships are competitive, and availability varies by program, department, and funding.
Eligibility Criteria
Students must meet the following criteria:
Minimum 3.0 GPA for master’s students.
Minimum 3.2 GPA for doctoral students.
Generally must be fully admitted to a graduate degree program. Non-degree students and students exclusively in certificate programs are not eligible for assistantships.
Currently enrolled in at least 9 credits for full-time masters-level graduate assistantships, or 6 credits for part-time masters-level graduate assistantships.
Masters students are eligible for up to 4 semesters of Graduate Center funding.
Doctoral students are eligible for up to 8 semesters of Graduate Center funding.
The Graduate Center will evaluate exceptions to the semester limits on a case by case basis, with priority for masters students in degree programs exceeding 40 graduate-level credits.
Graduate Assistants (GA) and Doctoral Assistants (DA) may not work more than 20 hours per week. If a student holds another position, it may impact their eligibility.
Micro-Internships
The Graduate Center's Micro-Internship Program offers short-term, project-based opportunities that help students build professional experience, explore career paths, and apply what they’re learning in the classroom. Projects are developed in partnership with departments across Montclair. Learn more and find current openings.
How to Apply
Step 1: Watch your email for open micro-internship opportunities
When micro-internship applications are open, The Graduate Center will share opportunities with eligible graduate students by email and through our website.
The email will include a list of available projects, along with details such as the department, project description, expected hours, stipend amount and application instructions.
Step 2: Review the available projects
Read through the list of opportunities carefully to determine which projects align with your interests, experience, schedule and career goals.
Each micro-internship is different, so be sure to review the expectations for each opportunity before applying.
Step 3: Apply to each opportunity individually
Students must apply separately for each micro-internship they are interested in. Applying to one opportunity does not automatically place you in consideration for all available projects.
When applying, you should include an updated resume and a brief statement explaining why you are interested in the project and how your experience connects to the role.
Step 4: Wait for follow-up from the hiring department
Each department reviews applications and selects candidates directly. If you are selected to move forward, the department may contact you for an interview or additional information.
Eligibility Criteria
Students must meet the following criteria:
Are currently matriculated in a graduate degree program or a fully graduate-level certificate program.
Are in good academic standing, with:
A GPA of 3.0 or higher for master’s and graduate certificate students.
A GPA of 3.2 or higher for doctoral students.
Are enrolled in fully graduate-level courses, numbered 500 or higher, at the time the application is submitted.
Have at least 3 credits of program requirements, at the 500 level or higher, remaining as of the start date of the internship.
Have already earned their bachelor’s degree, if enrolled in a combined Bx/Mx program.
Are not enrolled in a certificate or credential program that includes undergraduate-level courses, numbered 100–400.
Are not currently receiving financial support as a Graduate Assistant, Doctoral Assistant or Doctoral Teaching Fellow, regardless of the number of weekly service hours.
Are not currently employed by the University in any capacity, including as full-time staff, part-time staff or temporary employees.
Note: Make sure to review any program preferences listed on each micro-internship posting. These preferences are not required to apply, but meeting them may strengthen the application and increase eligibility for that role.
Graduate Honor Society
Meet our latest inductees.
Alpha Epsilon Lambda (AEL) recognizes graduate students for excellence in scholarship and leadership. Students who have completed at least 18 graduate credits and have GPAs in the top 20% of their school or college are invited to join. Invitations are sent once each semester. Students can also apply to serve as President of Montclair’s AEL chapter. Contact ael@montclair.edu for more information.
How to Apply
Students are invited to apply for Alpha Epsilon Lambda (AEL) by The Graduate Center.
Invitations are emailed to eligible students twice per year. Once invited, students must complete the application and submit all required materials by the deadline listed in the invitation.
Please note that an invitation to apply does not guarantee membership. Membership is highly competitive, and applications are reviewed before students are formally admitted.
Newly admitted members are recognized at an induction ceremony, typically held in the fall semester. Each initiate receives lifetime membership in AEL, along with a lapel pin, honor cord and certificate.
Eligibility Criteria
Students may be eligible for Alpha Epsilon Lambda (AEL) if they meet the following criteria:
Are actively matriculated in a graduate degree program.
Have successfully completed 18 graduate credits.
Have achieved academic standing in the top 20th percentile of their college or school.
Have demonstrated leadership through on-campus or off-campus involvement while a graduate student.
Please note that membership is highly competitive. For the most recently inducted members, the average cumulative GPA was 3.947, calculated using only courses at the 500 level or higher.
Graduate Council
The Graduate Council is the University’s advisory body for graduate policy, student initiatives, and curriculum review. Student representatives are elected with Dean approval and serve as key partners in advancing graduate student priorities. These representatives serve as the voice of their peers, offering insight into the graduate student experience and helping shape University-wide discussions. Learn more about Graduate Council and see upcoming meetings.
How to Apply
Selection processes vary by college. Contact your dean’s office to ask about current openings, the selection process and the term of service.
Eligibility Criteria
Student representatives should be able to:
Attend monthly Council meetings
Review materials before meetings and contribute to discussion
Gather input from graduate students in their college.
Share relevant Council updates with the students they represent
Your college or school may have additional requirements and expectations.
Graduate Student Travel Fund
Through the Student Research & Conference Travel Fund (SRCTF) Award, The Graduate Center provides modest funding to support professional development activities, including presenting research at a conference or traveling to gather research data. Funding is available to students enrolled in degree programs for the current academic year. Activities must be conducted as part of your Montclair degree program and mentored by a Montclair faculty member. View the application form.
How to Apply
Submit the application and required supporting materials at least one month before travel. All applications must be submitted by the stated deadline for the current academic year. Your application packet should include:
Completed application form
Letter of recommendation, addressed to The Graduate Center, from the Montclair faculty member supervising your research or conference presentation
Conference information
Proof of acceptance for presentation
Current resume/CV
If applicable, a copy of your approved IRB form
If applicable, information about other travel support requested and received
The Graduate Center will email you with the status of your request. Do not assume an expense is approved until you receive a decision. Students should keep itemized receipts and follow the reimbursement instructions provided with the award.
Eligibility Criteria
Open to graduate students in good standing
Master’s students must have a GPA of 3.0 or higher
Doctoral students must have a GPA of 3.2 or higher
You must be the presenting author at the conference, or traveling to conduct research for your thesis, dissertation, or capstone
Travel must take place between July 1 and June 30 of the current academic year
Students may receive this award up to three times during their graduate career
Students may receive the award no more than once per academic year
Please Note
Funding is limited and awarded on a first-come, first-served basis
Awards are up to $500, and the amount is based on the estimated costs submitted in your application
Incomplete applications will not be reviewed
This award provides partial support and may not cover the full cost of travel, so plan accordingly
Graduate Student Event Fund
The Graduate Center is excited to offer graduate students the opportunity to ideate, design, and execute their own events and programming for the graduate community. Through the Graduate Student Event Proposal Fund, students can propose workshops, trainings, orientations, networking events, or special programs to be offered by or co-sponsored by The Graduate Center. Submit a proposal.
How to Apply
Submit a proposal that explains the purpose, audience, format, proposed date, partners, logistics and estimated budget. Apply before making purchases, signing agreements or promising funds to a speaker or vendor.
Eligibility Criteria
You must be a currently enrolled Montclair State University graduate student.
The proposed event must be designed primarily for Montclair graduate students.
You must be prepared to organize the event from start to finish, including the budget, logistics, coordination, setup and day-of operations. If you have an idea but don't have the time, use our event suggestion form instead.
The proposal must be submitted at least four weeks before an online event or six weeks before an in-person event requiring space, materials or supplies.
Funding requests may not exceed $5,000 and must include an itemized budget with a clear justification for each expense.
The event and any related expenses or communications must receive Graduate Center approval before arrangements, purchases or promotion can begin.
Research Grants
The Office of Sponsored Programs (OSP) supports graduate students pursuing external funding for research, education, training and other scholarly activities. OSP can provide guidance on funding requirements, proposal development, University approvals and compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
How to Apply
Eligibility varies by funding opportunity. Review the individual grant or award details to confirm whether graduate students may apply and whether a faculty mentor, program approval or other University sponsor is required.
Eligibility Criteria
Review the individual grant or award application instructions for required materials, deadlines and submission steps. Contact OSP when University review or approval is required before submitting an application.
Student Research Symposium
The Student Research Symposium gives graduate students an opportunity to share their research and scholarship with the Montclair community through a poster presentation. Students can present their research questions, methods and findings while connecting with peers, faculty and attendees across disciplines.
How to Apply
The symposium is open to all current Montclair State University graduate students. Individual and interdisciplinary projects are welcome, and proposals that explore issues across multiple fields are encouraged.
Eligibility Criteria
Review the symposium submission instructions for proposal requirements, deadlines and poster guidelines. Selected participants must prepare a single poster and be available during the session to discuss their project and answer questions.
More Employment Opportunities
Graduate students can explore a variety of employment opportunities both on and off campus. The platforms below highlight current job openings, internships, and professional roles available to Montclair students and alumni.
Handshake
Handshake is the University’s career platform for discovering on- and off-campus jobs, internships, and networking opportunities. Make sure to check the eligibility criteria includes graduate students.
Access Handshake with your NetID to explore current opportunities.
Montclair State University Careers
The Montclair State University Human Resources website lists full-time, part-time, and staff positions available across the University. Graduate students and alumni may find additional employment opportunities posted through the University’s official job portal.
Explore current job openings through Montclair’s Human Resources website.
